ABC Next up was the Instant Dance Challenge, a much-dreaded round that's become an annual staple since it was first introduced in Season 33 . Each pair spent the week rehearsing a few different styles they could be asked to perform on the finale, but they didn't actually learn the style or corresponding song that they'd selected until five minutes before they danced live on the episode.

I've always enjoyed seeing the slightly unhinged challenge ideas that the "Dancing With the Stars" creatives cook up — I'm bummed that the potential Mega Dance round, which executive producer Conrad Green teased to me ahead of Season 35 , never materialized for this cycle — but I don't know that the season finale is the right place for the Instant Dance Challenge. Surely the finalists are already bundles of nerves heading into this last episode, and instead of showing off one more routine in which they feel very secure, they're left to half-panic their way through one of their final opportunities to prove to the voters how far they've come. entertainment.body:
Ezra Frech proved nothing can stop him when he flawlessly recovered from his prosthetic leg falling off during his “Dancing With the Stars” Season 35 finale freestyle with his pro partner, Daniella Karagach.

Despite his starting the routine with the prosthetic off, once he put it on he soon lost it after jumping down the stairs onto the ballroom floor as Linkin Park’s “Numb” played.

Frech was able to quickly get his prosthetic leg back on and finish the routine — which included wheelchair dancers on top of incredible choreography — with Karagach.

“His prosthetic was not supposed to come off, but what an incredible recovery,” co-host Alfonso Ribeiro said after the routine.

“Ezra, you are a hero,” Derek Hough said during the judges’ critiques, with Carrie Ann Inaba praising Karagach for “creating a whole new vocabulary” of dance.

The routine earned Frech and Karagach a 30/30, bringing their finale score to a perfect 90/90. They went on to win the season , taking home the Len Goodman Mirrorball Trophy.

“I want it to be a celebration of what is possible when you’re different,” Frech said in a pre-performance package, getting emotional discussing how Karagach — who called him her “best friend” — has embraced his prosthetic leg.

“The song is about breaking stereotypes. No sob story, this is all about power,” Frech said, revealing the routine will feature “talented wheelchair dancers because we want to change the way people see disability through this dance.”

entertainment.title: Matthew Capper, Late Music Publishing Exec, Honored With New Award
entertainment.summary: The Matthew Capper Award recognizes "individuals whose dedication and actions strengthen the music publishing community for future generations."
entertainment.body:
SYDNEY, Australia — Matthew Capper is saluted with a new, annual award which bears his name.

Announced Wednesday, Nov. 25, the Matthew Capper Award recognizes integrity, generosity, professionalism, commitment and service to music publishing in Australia and New Zealand, and is presented by the Australasian Music Publishers’ Association Limited (AMPAL).

Capper, the long-time former Warner Chappell Australia managing director and AMPAL chair, died unexpectedly in January 2025 following a surgical procedure. He was 47, just one month shy of his 48th birthday. Related Chris Brown Agrees to Increase Child Support -- For Now -- to Ex Diamond in Bitter Custody Fight Bill Donahue

“Matthew was widely respected for his integrity, professionalism, intelligence, humor, generosity and unwavering commitment to creators and the music publishing community,” reads a statement from AMPAL, announcing the new honor.

“A passionate advocate for music publishing, Matthew believed in the importance of doing things properly, ethically and in service of the broader industry. His approach to professional life reflected a belief that lasting contributions are measured not simply by individual achievements, but by the positive difference we make to those around us.”

In 2005, Capper became the youngest person ever appointed to the AMCOS board at the age of just 28. Two years later, in 2007, he became the youngest to join the APRA board, at 30.

He went on to serve as AMPAL chair for 11 years, as a non-executive director of APRA and AMCOS for more than 16 years, and as GM and managing director of Warner Chappell for over 20 years. On the international front, he served as a non-executive director and treasurer of the ICMP global board and as chair of ICMP’s Asia-Pacific Board.

The inaugural Matthew Capper Award, reads the AMPAL statement, honors his legacy by spotlighting “individuals whose dedication and actions strengthen the music publishing community for future generations.”

During the last day of principal photography on Avengers: Doomsday , revered actor Patrick Stewart , who reprised his role of Professor Charles Xavier for the film, stood up and gave a moving speech to the cast and crew. It would be his last day on a film set anywhere, according to his colleagues.

“We didn’t know necessarily it would be his last day on a set, but he was sort of indicating to us that he thought it was,” Marvel Studios president Kevin Feige said in an interview with Entertainment Weekly .

Anthony and Joe Russo, who helmed the last two Avengers films, 2018’s Infinity War and 2019’s Endgame , also felt the impact of the celebrated actor’s words that day. “I think it was in the back of all of our heads, we may never see him on set again,” Anthony told the outlet, calling the atmosphere that day as “very emotional.”

When addressing those he had worked side-by-side with, Stewart highlighted his character Xavier, whose empathy for others offered a source of comfort and security. “It was clear that he was struggling with his health, and he worked so hard to deliver a performance and a presence — for us as directors, for his other actors, for the crew,” Anthony said. “It was someone who was really being challenged in a very deep way on a health level, showing up and doing that. For him to have muscled through and delivered the performance that he did in that movie, and the experience that he delivered for all of us as collaborators, it made it intensely emotional.”

Feige confirmed to EW that he and the Russos are working on planning a tribute to Stewart. “We’re long done filming that movie, and he did an amazing job for us,” he said. “We’re looking now at how we can put something together that honors and respects our friend.”

entertainment.body:
While we're getting ready to shop until we drop on Black Friday , let's not forget about what comes first: Thanksgiving . The holiday that's all about food and family can also come with a side of stress, especially if you're hosting.

We chatted exclusively with Violet Witchel , content creator and cookbook author, whose dense bean salads have totally transformed how I think about meal prepping for the week. And she came through with the best tips to help us with hosting, prepping food and even being a great holiday guest!

But if you're feeling stressed about your Thanksgiving menu and how you can get all the cooking and prep work done in time for dinner... don't be! Because guess what, even chefs like Violet pick up a few pre-made ingredients to help save time.

"Pre-made pie crust, mixes - like if you're going to make cornbread, get cornbread mix. Canned cranberry sauce, totally fine," she said of the items she'd get from the store. "Pre-bought stuffing, like the mix, totally fine. Pre-minced vegetables, totally fine."

But one thing you won't catch her using? Powdered mashed potatoes. "I think on Thanksgiving, you've gotta do that from scratch."

And whether you're team pumpkin, apple or pecan, supporting a local bakery is not only tasty but also a time-saver she added. Don't forget the canned whipped cream and your favorite ice cream!

For more food prep advice and tips from Violet, keep reading!

"I don't love to bring wine because I feel like everyone brings wine and they feel kind of obligated to serve it at dinner," Violet shared. "So I love to bring a nice bottle of olive oil because it's one of those things you're like 'oh, this is wonderful to have.' "

entertainment.title: How to Watch F1 Like a Pro, According to McLaren Drivers Lando Norris and Oscar Piastri
entertainment.summary: The drivers share tips for new fans, while touting T-Mobile's technology creating immersive touchpoints for a better viewing experience
entertainment.body:
If you purchase an independently reviewed product or service through a link on our website, Rolling Stone may receive an affiliate commission.

As the 2026 F1 season made its final U.S. stop of the year, Las Vegas once again turned its neon-lit streets into an impressive, 17-turn race that wound its way through The Strip, with drivers whizzing past the city’s most iconic landmarks. On Sunday, Max Verstappen took home the checkered flag at the Formula 1 Las Vegas Grand Prix after a nail-biting finish, with McLaren’s Lando Norris and Oscar Piastri posting a double-podium finish to complete the top three.

With F1’s growing prominence in the U.S., new fans continue to enter the high-speed world of racing. But while the rules of Formula 1 seem simple enough — the first car to pass the checkered flag after 50-odd laps, wins — it does take some time to truly understand the complexities of the sport.

Rolling Stone sat down with McLaren drivers Oscar Piastri and Lando Norris ahead of the Las Vegas Grand Prix to glean some tips on how new fans can optimize their viewing experience.

Norris advises the audience to watch onboard videos and listen to the commentators who make the race more understandable. “When you then see the onboard cameras in the driver’s eye [line], I think it looks a lot more realistic [since] that is what I’m seeing with my head,” he says, “So I think that gives a much better experience. The more that they can do that, and get the sensation of speed, the easier it will be for people to understand.”

And while new viewers might only focus on the leaderboard, Piastri begs to differ. “I think the first thing about Formula 1 is not everyone’s car is the same, so I think just because some people aren’t winning, it doesn’t necessarily mean that they’re worse than the people that are winning,” he says. “Oftentimes the racing in the midfield can sometimes be more entertaining than the racing at the front.”

The drivers both say that strategy shifts within varying climate conditions, tire compounds and their impact to performance and longevity, and the car’s on-track behavior are just a few of the factors being considered on the sidelines during every race.

As part of their preparation, the team reviews prior races of the current season, as well as footage of the same track last year to see any learnings that could apply. Norris emphasizes how the addition of new cameras showing extra angles on the track can help the driver’s pre-race POV while adding to the immersive fan experience.

Jerry (Jerry Seinfeld) and George Costanza (Jason Alexander) are holding auditions for their show-within-a-show. Melissa auditions for the role based on Elaine Benes (Julia Louise Dreyfuss).

She enters saying that the hallway was like a "bald convention," which noticeably annoys George. Melissa apologizes, resulting in Jerry playing it off by saying George "knows he's bald." She follows her apology by wondering if a man in the hallway wears sweatpants routinely. This is the last straw for George, whom Jerry recently made fun of for wearing sweatpants in public. After Melissa reads just a few lines with Jerry, George ends the audition by curtly thanking Melissa.

While Hargitay was only on the show for less than a minute, her performance was memorable. George's insecurities, which made for some good running gags, were inadvertently triggered by her casual comments. Jerry's immediate attraction to her, to the extent that he insisted on reading the part with her, was also classic for his character.

CBS/YouTube Audiences of the 1990s may remember the short-lived sitcom "Can't Hurry Love." The CBS series lasted only one season before being canceled. It centered on Annie O'Donnell (Nancy McKeon), an employment agency worker trying to sweeten her dating life. One of her best friends on the show was the energetic Didi Edelstein, played by Mariska Hargitay.

sports.summary: One of the best Thanksgiving games ever will take place Thursday in Detroit.
sports.body:
When the Lions host the Bears, it will be the first time in NFL history that two teams on winning streaks of five games or longer meet on Thanksgiving. The Lions are on a six-game winning streak and the Bears are on a five-game winning streak.

The Lions and Bears are both 8-2 and tied for first place in the NFC North, so the game has major playoff implications. The winner will be all alone in first place in the best division in football.

This will be the 21st time the Bears and Lions have met on Thanksgiving. The Bears have an 11-9 edge in the previous 20 games.

sports.title: Broncos face quick pivot to preparing for Mason Rudolph on Friday
sports.summary: The Black Friday game between the Broncos and Steelers was preceded by the Black Tuesday benching of quarterback Aaron Rodgers.
sports.body:
As one source put it, the Broncos aren’t sure whether the unexpected move is a good thing or a bad thing.

Obviously, Rodgers has slipped. But the Steelers were 6-4. They had gone all in with the first-ballot Hall of Famer, for a second straight year. The notion that they’d pull the rug out from under Rodgers and ride with Rudolph is jarring.

Quarterbacks on winning teams don’t get benched very often. In 2004, the Giants sat Hall of Famer Kurt Warner despite a 5-4 record. But the goal then was to get rookie Eli Manning on the field. For the Steelers, they’ve made the decision that Rudolph, a veteran backup 19 regular-season starts in eight years, gives them a better chance to win.

The element of surprise could be a factor in the timing, too. It’s possible that the Steelers considered not saying anything at all.

That would have been hard to pull off. Unless coach Mike McCarthy had been able to get everyone (including Rodgers) to clam up, word would have gotten out that Rudolph was getting the first-team reps at practice.

This story is just getting started. Rodgers will surely have a reaction. And it surely won’t be a shrug of the shoulders and an acceptance that he won’t even be in uniform for the game.

sports.title: Steelers bench Aaron Rodgers for Mason Rudolph
sports.summary: Announcement comes out of the blue, after 11:00 p.m. ET on Tuesday night.
sports.body:
The team has announced — after 11:00 p.m. ET on Tuesday night — that Mason Rudolph will start at quarterback on Friday against the Broncos. Rodgers will be inactive for the game.

It’s a stunning move. And it’s not because Rodgers has an injury. He did not appear on Tuesday’s official practice report.

On Monday, coach Mike McCarthy was asked whether one of the three other quarterbacks could be used at some point to mix things up. Once McCarthy understood the import of the question, he said unequivocally, “ Aaron Rodgers is our quarterback .”

The next question is whether the team will release Rodgers, and whether he’ll ask to be released.

Why wouldn’t he want his freedom, if he’s not playing? If/when he clears waivers, he’d have the ability to sit and wait for an opportunity to arise with a contender, likely if an injury to the starter happens.

Regardless, it’s an unexpected and frankly seismic move during what is Rodgers’s final season. The fact that the Steelers held the information until late Tuesday night shows that they appreciate the significance of the move.

“Do you think that bothers me?” Sanders said at a Tuesday press conference, via the Associated Press. “Do you think that causes me to lose sleep or rest? Do you think that affects or impacts my life?

“That don’t affect me like it may affect you or may affect some others. Because I’m in the third quarter of life. I may be losing games, but I’m winning life .”

He’d win again, even if he’s fired. Colorado would owe him a buyout of $25.5 million. And he’d then be available to coach elsewhere.

Her husband, William Clay Ford, bought the Lions in 1963. When he died in 2014, Martha Firestone Ford became the owner of the team. In 2020, she relinquished control of the team to her daughter, Sheila Ford Hamp.

Mrs. Ford is survived by her four children, her 14 grandchildren, and 17 great-grandchildren.

Born in Akron, Ohio, Mrs. Ford was the granddaughter of Harvey S. Firestone, founder of the Firestone Tire and Rubber Company.

We extend our condolences to Mrs. Ford’s family, friends, and the entire Lions organization.

It ended up being the most-watched Week 11 Sunday night game since 2013. And, if the game had been more competitive, the final number would have been higher.

Indeed, the game averaged 27.6 million during the 9:00 p.m. ET to 9:15 p.m. ET window, before the game was essentially over.

sports.title: Thanksgiving week features extra episodes of #PFTPM
sports.summary: Thanksgiving week typically alters the usual PFT Live schedule.
sports.body:
Like every year, PFT Live shuts down on Thanksgiving and Black Friday. After weeks of five two-hour shows every Monday through Friday, the crew deserves a break on the two days that most of the rest of the world takes a break.

Enter #PFTPM. If you’ve noticed (or if you haven’t), we’ve significantly increased #PFTPM this season. It’s a YouTube exclusive, with some of the clips landing in PFT posts.

This week, new #PFTPM episodes will land on Wednesday afternoon (the usual weekly nuggets episode), on Friday (a review of the three Thanksgiving games plus anything else of interest), the usual Saturday episode, and the pair of Sunday editions reviewing the early afternoon and late afternoon windows.

We’ll also be trying something new. With the NFL staging a Thanksgiving Eve game for the first time (Packers-Rams), I’ll be taping a reaction to the game immediately after it ends at or about 11:30 p.m. ET.

If nothing else, it will keep me from consuming excessive amounts of adult beverages during the game. Or not, which will make the episode even more interesting.

sports.summary: YouTube's on-again, off-again arrangements to stream select NFL games may be on again.
sports.body:
This year, Christmas Eve lands on a Thursday; Prime Video will televise the Texans-Eagles game that night (barring a flex). Next year, Christmas Eve lands on a Friday.

YouTube was at one point negotiating the five-game package for 2026 that landed with Netflix. It includes Wednesday night’s first-of-its-kind Thanksgiving Eve game between the Packers and Rams. YouTube walked, as Ourand reported at the time, when the league tried to split the five-game package between multiple partners.

The arrangement between the NFL and YouTube currently includes Sunday Ticket. That package could be disappearing in the next round of broadcast deals.

The inevitable expansion of the regular season to 18 games per team will create another 16 games that can be sliced and diced into special packages.

sports.title: Sam LaPorta upgraded to full participation at Lions practice
sports.summary: Lions tight end Sam LaPorta took a step in the right direction on Tuesday's injury report.

The Lions listed LaPorta as a full participant after listing him as limited with an ankle injury on Monday. Both reports were estimations because the Lions only held walkthroughs the last two days.

Safety Chuck Clark (hamstring) moved to a limited listing after being listed as out to start the week.

Defensive end DJ Wonnum (back) and cornerback Ennis Rakestraw (shoulder) were listed as out of practice for the second straight day. Defensive lineman Skylar Gill-Howard (knee) was also out and head coach Dan Campbell announced earlier in the day that he’ll miss the rest of the season.

Cornerbacks Khalil Dorsey (wrist) and cornerback D.J. Reed (hip) were both full participants.

sports.summary: Bills reveal familiar Thanksgiving uniforms ahead of Thursday night's matchup against Kansas City.

sports.title: Brandon Aiyuk will visit Commanders
sports.summary: Aiyuk has mentioned signing with Washington for months.
sports.body:
The former 49ers receiver cleared waivers on Tuesday. Agent Drew Rosenhaus told ESPN that Aiyuk is scheduled to visit the Commanders on Wednesday.

Aiyuk has been linked to the Commanders for months. He played college football at Arizona State with quarterback Jayden Daniels. Commanders G.M. Adam Peters worked for the 49ers when Aiyuk arrived as a first-round pick in 2020.

And the Commanders — a sudden contender in the NFC East — could use some help at the position.

Aiyuk has been vocal about his desire to play for the Commanders. It got a little dicey during Aiyuk’s social-media tirade over the summer; a couple of his attacks were targeted at Daniels.

Regardless, the Commanders will be getting the first crack at Aiyuk, who is extra motivated to sign a contract and to start playing, especially after the 49ers delayed his free agency for two weeks after he was reinstated by the league from the reserve/left squad list.

sports.title: Bears add CB Isaac Yiadom off waivers
sports.summary: The Bears have added a defensive back.
sports.body:
Chicago has claimed cornerback Isaac Yiadom off waivers, the team announced on Tuesday.

The cornerback appeared in three games for the Commanders this season, playing exclusively on special teams.

Bears defensive coordinator Dennis Allen has plenty of familiarity with Yiadom, as the cornerback played under him when Allen was New Orleans’ head coach in 2022 and 2023.

A Broncos third-round pick in 2018, Yiadom has played 121 career games with 34 starts for the Broncos, Giants, Packers, Texans, Saints, 49ers, and Commanders.

sports.title: Michigan does about-face on Trev Alberts, potentially owing him $17.2 million
sports.summary: The last time Trev Alberts made this kind of a stir, he was the subject of Bill Tobin's legendary rant against Mel Kiper.
sports.body:
This time, the situation potentially involves a significant payment to Alberts.

Via ESPN, Michigan backed out of an agreement to hire Alberts (who played in only 29 career games over three seasons after being the fifth overall pick in the 1994 draft) to become the university’s next athletic director. Alberts told ESPN that he had signed a “binding memorandum of understanding” for the position.

Alberts’s lawyer, Tom Mars, told ESPN that Michigan owes Alberts a $17.2 million buyout.

For that kind of money, Michigan will be very tempted to refuse to pay, forcing litigation and the expense, uncertainty, and delay that goes along with it. Alberts could decide to take less than he’s owed, simply to end the fight.

Of course, Alberts also could become determined to prove a point — if he and Mars believe Alberts has an ironclad claim to the money.

Michigan’s about-face apparently relates to deposition testimony from Alberts in a Title IX case arising from his tenure at Nebraska. Per ESPN, Alberts gave testimony on December 4, 2025, that Michigan regards as problematic.

Alberts was asked whether he believes it’s true that college coaches should never have sex with the athletes they’re coaching. The obvious answer is, “Yes.” Alberts pursued a different strategy.

He then said the situation could be “nuanced,” due to preexisting relationships or eligibility waivers that could result in athletes being nearly the same age as young assistant coaches.

sports.title: Giants put Greg Newsome on injured reserve
sports.summary: Giants head coach John Harbaugh said on Monday that cornerback Greg Newsome will miss multiple weeks with a high-ankle sprain and a clearer picture of just how many weeks came on Tuesday.
sports.body:
Newsome was placed on the injured reserve list, which means he’ll be out for at least the next four games. Newsome signed a one-year deal with the Giants in the offseason and signed a three-year extension earlier this month.

Paulson Adebo is expected to see more playing time with Newsome out of the lineup.

The Giants filled Newsome’s roster spot by signing linebacker Dawuane Smoot off of the practice squad. He has appeared in three games and had three tackles and a sack in those appearances.

sports.title: Player-turned-doctor Laurent Duvernay-Tardif is working with the Chiefs' medical staff
sports.summary: Former Chiefs offensive lineman Laurent Duvernay-Tardif, who got his medical degree while playing in the NFL, is back in Kansas City working with the Chiefs' medical staff.
sports.body:
“Feeling privileged to be back on the sidelines, this time shadowing the medical team to gain experience in sports medicine and on-field emergency response,” Duvernay-Tardif wrote on social media.

A native of Quebec who has been completing medical training there since retiring from the NFL, Duvernay-Tardif is currently spending a month with the Chiefs’ medical staff to learn more about treatment of athletes.

Listed at 6-foot-5 and 321 pounds during his playing days, Duvernay-Tardif appears to have lost weight and blended in on the sideline during Sunday’s Chiefs game, although CBS briefly showed him on camera.

Duvernay-Tardif was a starter for the Chiefs from 2015 to 2019. He chose not to play in 2020, instead lending his medical expertise to covid patients. He returned and played for the Jets in 2021 and 2022.

sports.title: Sean Payton suspends J.K. Dobbins for Week 12 for conduct detrimental to the team
sports.summary: Dobbins played just one offensive snap in the Week 11 win over the Raiders.
sports.body:
Head coach Sean Payton announced in his Tuesday press conference that Dobbins has been suspended one game for conduct detrimental to the team.

Payton did not elaborate or answer any follow-up questions, though he did note that the suspension was his decision.

Dobbins began the season as Denver’s starting running back but has now filled that role in just one of the last four games, with rookie Jonah Coleman taking over as the Broncos’ lead back.

Coleman rushed for 111 yards on 24 carries with three touchdowns and caught four passes for 18 yards in Sunday’s victory over the Raiders.

Dobbins was on the field for just one offensive snap in Week 11, taking a carry that was stuffed for no gain.

In 10 games with seven starts this season, Dobbins has rushed for 324 yards with three touchdowns and caught nine passes for 31 yards.

sports.title: Brandon Aiyuk is a free agent after clearing waivers
sports.summary: Wide receiver Brandon Aiyuk is officially a free agent.
sports.body:
Aiyuk went unclaimed around the league after the 49ers placed him on waivers Monday, which means that he’s now free to sign a contract with any club. It was the expected result as any team claiming Aiyuk would also inherit his contract.

Aiyuk expressed interest in signing with the Commanders during his extended impasse with the 49ers and the path is now clear for that to happen. Given how long Aiyuk has been off of the field, it would seem likely that his stint with his next team will begin on the practice squad.

There’s no word about a deal at this point, but things can develop quickly now that Aiyuk is free to sign.

sports.body: The Buffalo Bills suddenly have two vacant spots on their practice squad. Core pieces of said practice squad, quarterback Shane Buechele and 2025 sixth-round pick Chase Lundt, were added to the 53-man rosters of other teams in separate transactions on Tuesday before the club’s Week 12 Thanksgiving contest against the Chiefs. First it was Buechele: [Media: https://twitter.com/AdamSchefter/status/2125319223455215868?a=k48cEgeesAAWtA1pZGk&s=20] Given the Colts released Daniel Jones on November 20, they were in need of more quarterback depth behind former first-rounder Anthony Richardson, who’s become the team’s starter. Buechle is presumed to be Indianapolis’ new No. 3 quarterback behind Richardson and Riley Leonard. Buechele spent from 2023 - 2025 with the Bills before re-signing in Buffalo in January 2026. Under 20 minutes later, it was reported that Lundt was on the move too: [Media: https://twitter.com/TomPelissero/status/2125323896421511186?a=4r4MJdm1Jq7U7WwUMwc&s=20] The Seahawks are dealing with injuries to newly acquired guard Quenton Nelson, longtime right tackle Abraham Lucas, and franchise left tackle Charles Cross. The former sixth-round pick failed to appear in a regular-season game for the Bills but played over 300 preseason snaps the past two summers after a collegiate career at UConn. Who do you think the Bills should add to their practice squad after losing Buechele and Lundt?

sports.title: Kenneth Walker limited in his return to Chiefs practice
sports.summary: Walker missed the last two games with a groin injury.
sports.body:
Walker has missed the last two games with a groin injury, but his return to work would seem to open the door to a return to the lineup against the Bills on Thursday night.

Walker ran 159 times for 872 yards and seven touchdowns in eight games before the injury. He also has 26 catches for 172 yards and four touchdowns.

Tight end Noah Gray also returned to practice which left right tackle Jaylon Moore (ankle) was the only Chief out of practice. Defensive tackle Omarr Norman-Lott (knee) was listed as limited while Gray (rib), cornerback Mansoor Delane (shoulder), wide receiver Rashee Rice (knee), right guard Trey Smith (concussion), and defensive lineman Peter Woods (neck) were full participants.

sports.title: Panthers do not activate Brady Christensen at expiration of 21-day practice window
sports.summary: As it turns out, the Panthers will not have one of their offensive linemen return for the 2026 season.
sports.body:
Via Alex Zietlow of the Charlotte Observer , Carolina did not activate offensive lineman Brady Christensen to the 53-man roster, allowing his 21-day practice window to expire.

That means Christensen will revert to being on injured reserve and is ineligible to return to the team’s roster in 2026.

Christensen suffered a hamstring injury in August after suffering a torn Achilles in the middle of the 2025 season.

A Panthers third-round pick in 2021, Christensen has appeared in 59 career games with 34 starts.

sports.title: Jake Ferguson, Tyler Booker remain out of practice for Cowboys
sports.summary: The Cowboys upgraded the practice participation of a couple of players on Tuesday's injury report, but two offensive starters remained out.
sports.body:
Right guard Tyler Booker (ankle) and tight end Jake Ferguson (knee, ankle) were listed as non-participants for the second straight day. Ferguson has missed the last two games and Booker was out against the Titans last Sunday, so it seems unlikely either will play against the Eagles on Thanksgiving.

Linebackers Jaishawn Barham (hip, groin) and Dee Winters (knee) both returned as limited participants. Barham did not play against the Titans, but Winters had two tackles.

Wide receiver Jonathan Mingo (ankle) was downgraded to out and safety P.J. Locke (concussion) was limited for the second straight day. sports.title: Eagles sign LB Chance Campbell, waive C Jake Majors
sports.summary: The Eagles made a couple of changes to their roster ahead of Thursday's game against the Cowboys.
sports.body:
The team announced that they have signed linebacker Chance Campbell off of their practice squad. They waived center Jake Majors in a corresponding move.

Campbell has appeared in one game this season. He played 11 special teams snaps and made one tackle in Week 3. Campbell also played in four games for the Titans during the 2023 season.

Majors started two games earlier this season while the Eagles were dealing with a number of injuries on the offensive line. Drew Kendall is now handling center duties for the Eagles.

sports.title: Seahawks add Chase Lundt off Bills practice squad, waive CB Avery Smith
sports.summary: The Seahawks are making a pair of roster moves on Tuesday.
sports.body:
Per Tom Pelissero of Netflix, Seattle is signing offensive tackle Chase Lundt off of Buffalo’s practice squad.

As a corresponding roster move, the team is waiving cornerback Avery Smith.

Lundt, 26, was a sixth-round pick in 2025. He’s appeared in two career games, playing three offensive snaps and five special teams snaps.

Smith appeared in six games for Seattle this season, playing exclusively on special teams.

The Buffalo Bills remain in control of their playoff fate thanks to an AFC-best 9-1 record. In their first six games, Buffalo’s defense allowed 171 points, giving up an average of 28.5 for last in the NFL in scoring defense. In the four games since the bye, that figure has plummeted to 37 points — an average of 9.3 points per game. sports.title: Dan Quinn on Stefon Diggs: I love his fire
sports.summary: Monday night ended well for the Commanders, but the start of the game was rough for the team's offense and frustrations about that boiled over on the sideline at one point.
sports.body:
Wide receiver Stefon Diggs was caught by ESPN cameras yelling in the direction of quarterback Jayden Daniels and lip readers shared that he appeared to be telling him to “throw the f—-king ball” after a sack ended a Washington drive in the second quarter. The Commanders bounced back with a touchdown the next time they got the ball and wound up with a 22-20 win on a last-second field goal.

The result made it easier to gloss over any bad feelings that cropped up earlier in the evening and head coach Dan Quinn said on Tuesday that he has no issue with Diggs using his voice in that manner.

“I love his fire , I do,” Quinn said, via John Keim of ESPN.com. “I love that. There’s a lot of good that comes with it where it can sound like he’s mad but it’s like some energy that comes behind it.”

Quinn added that “if something didn’t feel right I would step in and address it,” but that the current mindset in Washington appears to be all’s well that ends well.

sports.title: Titans have only defense in the NFL giving up scores on most of its drives
sports.summary: The Titans' defense allowed the Cowboys' offense to score on every drive on Sunday, with the exception of a kneeldown at the end of the game.
sports.body:
Tennessee’s defense has now given up a score on 50.5 percent of opposing possessions this season. The Titans are the only defense in the league that gives up points most of the time it takes the field.

Over the last two games, the Titans’ defense went on an incredible run: In addition to giving up scores on the Cowboys’ first eight offensive possessions in Week 11, the Titans gave up points on the Jaguars’ last five possessions in Week 10. That streak of 13 consecutive drives giving up scores is the longest streak of consecutive drives in which any NFL defense has given up points, for as far back as full drive data is available.

The Titans’ defense’s last 14 drives ended in 10 touchdowns, three field goals and a kneeldown.

Titans coach Robert Saleh has had success as a defensive coordinator, but he went 20-36 in his previous stint as head coach of the Jets, and he’s now 1-9 with the Titans. When he’s the head coach, his defenses don’t get the job done.

sports.title: Colts sign QB Shane Buechele off Bills practice squad
sports.summary: The Colts have added a third quarterback to their active roster.
sports.body:
The team announced on Tuesday that they have signed Shane Buechele off of the Bills’ practice squad. He will slot in as the third quarterback in Indianapolis behind Anthony Richardson and Riley Leonard.

Buechele has been with the Bills for most of the last four seasons, but he did have a brief stint on the Chiefs’ roster after Patrick Mahomes was injured last year. He made his regular season debut for Kansas City during that stint and went 7-of-14 for 88 yards in Week 18.

The Colts also announced that they have signed veteran defensive end Carl Lawson off of their practice squad. They placed defensive end Caden Curry on injured reserve and waived offensive tackle Charlie Heck in corresponding moves.

sports.title: Ravens waive returner LaJohntay Wester
sports.summary: After he had a rough Sunday in Charlotte, the Ravens are moving on from LaJohntay Wester.
sports.body:
Per Jeff Zrebiec of TheAthletic.com, Baltimore has waived Wester on Wednesday.

Wester muffed a pair of punts in the loss to the Panthers, with Carolina recovering one of them.

A sixth-round pick in last year’s draft, Wester averaged 8.2 yards per punt return and 23.7 yards per kick return in 11 games this season. He averaged 12.4 yards per punt return and 24.6 yards per kick return in 2025.

Wester also contributed five catches for 58 yards in 2026. But with four fumbles this season and three in the last three games, Baltimore has elected to move on.

sports.title: Packers activate Micah Parsons to 53-man roster
sports.summary: Signs continue to point toward Parsons making his 2026 debut against the Rams on Wednesday night.
sports.body:
Green Bay announced on Tuesday that Parsons has been activated to the 53-man roster in advance of Wednesday’s game against the Rams.

Parsons has been medically cleared to play. While he’s officially listed as questionable, all signs point to the edge rusher returning from his torn ACL this week in Los Angeles.

In 14 games for the Packers last year, Parsons tallied 12.5 sacks with 12 tackles for loss and 27 quarterback hits. He also had one pass defensed and two forced fumbles.

Though he wasn’t able to finish the 2025 season, he was still an AP first-team All-Pro for the third time in his career.

Green Bay had an open spot on its 53-man roster, so the club did not need to make a corresponding move.

sports.summary: As Thanksgiving Day quickly approaches, fans of the Buffalo Bills have plenty to be thankful for. The team has a 9-1 record and currently sits atop the standings in the AFC. Josh Allen remains and MVP candidate, James Cook is as good as ever, and Gregory Rousseau may be a Defensive Player of the Yea
sports.body: As Thanksgiving Day quickly approaches, fans of the Buffalo Bills have plenty to be thankful for. The team has a 9-1 record and currently sits atop the standings in the AFC. Josh Allen remains and MVP candidate, James Cook is as good as ever, and Gregory Rousseau may be a Defensive Player of the Year candidate. Now the Bills play the Kansas City Chiefs on Thanksgiving night at Highmark Stadium. To be honest, originally I was excited to see that the Bills were playing on Thanksgiving. It’s is arguably the second greatest football day of the year, behind opening day of the season. The Bills are in the prime-time slot, when all of the hustle and bustle of the holiday has passed, and I can relax that night for the game (at least as much as I can feel relaxed when the Bills play the Chiefs). But now that it is almost Thanksgiving, there is a big part of me that wishes the Bills were not playing on Thursday night. Maybe the matchup with the Chiefs has something to do with it. Playing one of your most hated rivals on a short week never feels right, granted the Bills are not the team that has to travel for the game. I usually find the match-ups with the Chiefs to be more stress-inducing, which might have much to do with this, too. The alternative would be falling asleep in a tryptophan-induced coma by halftime of the prime-time game. That would not be the worst thing, right? So how are you feeling about the Bills playing on Thanksgiving? Is it messing with your travel plans? Are you excited for the game? Will you be making the trip to Highmark Stadium? Be sure to share in the comments below, and I hope that everyone has a Happy Thanksgiving!

sports.body: On Sunday, the Jets traveled across the country and beat the Los Angeles Chargers on the road, snapping a five-game losing streak in the process. Ordinarily, a win like that would be met with plenty of positivity, especially considering the offense produced its highest EPA per drive performance in nearly 23 years. Instead, the result was met with a surprising amount of mixed emotions. Some of the reaction was downright negative. So what does this win actually mean? And more importantly, where do the Jets stand through 11 games? Let me start with the obvious. This team is not good. At 3-8, we’ve seen enough to establish that. I’m not going to pretend one win against the Chargers fundamentally changes anything. The defense is very bad from a talent standpoint and continues to perform poorly. Even against a relatively mediocre Chargers offense, there were plenty of disappointing moments. sports.body: The Buffalo Bills took care of business against an underdog on Sunday, beating the Miami Dolphins. The Jacksonville Jaguars and Cincinnati Bengals both lost to underdogs from the NFC East on Sunday and Monday, which paves the way for the Bills to clinch the number one seed in a new scenario. Yes, with seven games left it is premature to talk about clinching scenarios, but the Bills have a four-game lead in the AFC East plus two games left against the Jets and Dolphins. The division crown is heavily tilted toward the Bills now, and we are starting to look past that to the one seed. (The Bills are obvously focused one game at a time.) With the Jaguars and Bengals losing this week, the Bills now can win the rest of their AFC games and secure the overall record and the AFC record they would need to clinch the one seed, a status that has eluded them throughout Josh Allen’s entire career. Buffalo has games against the Kansas City Chiefs, Denver Broncos, and New England Patriots plus the Dolphins and Jets. Winning those five AFC contests gets them to 14 wins and an 11-1 AFC record with head-to-head tiebreakers over the Broncos and Chiefs. Denver and KC would both have three losses on account of losing to Buffalo. Meanwhile the Jaguars and Bengals could top out at 14-3 but have two AFC losses apiece. Even in a three-way tie scenario, the Bills would come out on top. In short, if the Bills win the rest of their AFC games, they can lose both games to the NFC North’s Chicago Bears and Green Bay Packers and still be the one seed in the AFC. (Winning those is preferable, but irrelevant here.) If the Bills stumble against an AFC opponent, obviously things will need to be recalibrated. sports.body: I think part of being a diehard NFL fan is trying to derive meaning out of everything that happens to a team, no matter how small. Think about the offseason program. How often do we have reports on which players are up and which players are down? These continue into training camp. Then the second half of preseason games produce deep dive analysis of which players are potentially hidden gems or important depth pieces. Every now and then an OTA, training camp, or preseason, breakout turns out to be a preview of a genuine step forward by a developing player. Far more often the players and the hype are forgotten. It also goes this way in late season games when a team has fallen out of the Playoff race. Can a loss help a team secure a high Draft pick to land a franchise changing player? Can a late season surge lead to momentum carrying into a future season and be the first step in instilling a new culture? In both cases the answer is yes. Far more often, however, these games don’t have a ton of meaning either way in the long run. They amount to a bad team playing out the string. The Jets’ Week 11 victory over the Chargers has evoked passions across the fanbase. Some fans are furious about the team hurting its NFL Draft positioning. Others are happy to get the win. I don’t think there’s a “right” or a “wrong” way to be a fan. Everybody wants the same thing in the end, for the Jets to have success. Opinions simply vary on the best way to get there. I can understand fans who are hoping for as high of a pick as possible. Of course, we have seen over and over that the quality of the coaching staff and front office making the pick are generally far more important than where the pick is made. Patrick Mahomes, Josh Allen, and Lamar Jackson were not the first quarterbacks selected in their respective Draft years. Taking it deeper, one study suggests the odds of the top player drafted at his position having a better career than the third player picked at the same position is only slightly better than a coin toss. Yes, there is the occasional case where losing helps a team land a player who legitimately changes everything, and there are cases where a meaningless late season win causes a team to miss out on that player. sports.body: It’s a beautiful victory, Monday, New York Jets fans! I’m sure everyone is happy about this dub, right? Wrong. The fan base is fractured down the middle with this result. Some fans are happy to see their team win for the first time in five weeks. While others are pulling their hair out over what they describe as a frustrating loss to a crappy opponent that screwed up their draft positioning. “A Jets win that feels like a loss to many people in the fan base, and I don’t blame anyone who feels that way because I feel the same way. Watching the Jets go out there and win this game just leaves that sinking feeling in your stomach oh my God they have ruined the tank again. That’s the feeling many in the fan base have, and if you feel that way, you’re not a bad fan because you see the forest through the trees because you understand that a win over a one-win Chargers team could potentially do more damage than good. If you’re going to win games, you want it to be because your young players are playing great, not because 33-year-old Sterling Shepard is scoring two touchdowns on his only two touches of the game,” ESPN New York’s Jake Asman lamented. The Jets were not going to finish 2-15. Anyone who set that expectation set themselves up for failure. They have been in a ton of close games this season. A broken clock is right twice a day. A blind squirrel can find a nut. The Jets were eventually going to stumble into a victory, and who knows if this is the last one. There are still six games left in the 2026 regular season.
